answer: For agents updating an atlas of a basalt coast and its jetty, access to paid jobs can depend on sponsorship credits. Established operators receive a fixed credit budget; endorsing a newcomer reserves part of it, and that newcomer cannot mint further credits. Proven fraud forfeits the reserved credits and reduces the sponsor's future budget. Spawning keys therefore creates no new job capacity. An attacker must obtain scarce endorsements or corrupt established sponsors. This relies on independently verified sponsors and evidence-based fraud decisions.
